title: Residents demonstrate in seven Kabul-province districts in support of the republic
location: Kuhdaman, Surobi, Khak Jabar, Deh Sabz, Chahar Asiab, Musahi and Paghman districts, Kabul Province
scope: Multiple localities in Kabul Province; whether the reports describe one coordinated event or separate district gatherings is unresolved.

threshold_50_evidence: The opened report’s qualitative “thousands” estimate is well above 50 if this was one coordinated event. title: Money changers gather over Central Bank licensing policy during nationwide strike
location: Outside Sarai Shahzada, Kabul, at the reported strike-start gathering; Salam Watandar also reports gatherings in Kabul and some unspecified provinces on Feb. 20.
scope: Reported nationwide sector strike with public gatherings in Kabul and some provinces; the assembly unit and geographic extent are unresolved.
organizer: Money changers nationwide; no named formal organizing body identified in the opened report.
threshold_50_evidence: Salam Watandar explicitly reports a public gathering outside Sarai Shahzada at the strike’s start and further protest gatherings in Kabul and some provinces on Feb. 20, but gives no attendance count. A nationwide work stoppage or number of businesses does not establish 50 assembled people.

title.summary: The Salam Watandar headline reports the nationwide money-changers’ strike ended.

start_date.summary: S003 directly places a public gathering at the strike start and gives both “16 days before Feb. 21” and “18 Dalw/Bahman” clues, which conflict at exact-day precision. S014 is published Feb. 6 (also shown as 18 Dalw 1399) and says nationwide work stopped from Saturday, but does not report a public gathering. Together the sources support February month precision only; S014 does not fix the assembly day.

end_date.summary: The article says the work strike ended after a Feb. 21 meeting, but does not document physical closure of the public gatherings.

location.summary: The opening gathering was in front of Sarai Shahzada in Kabul; further Feb. 20 gatherings are mentioned in Kabul and some unspecified provinces.

scope.summary: S003 calls the strike nationwide and reports gatherings at Sarai Shahzada and on Feb. 20 in Kabul and some provinces. S014 separately describes a nationwide work stoppage but gives no public-assembly details; national strike scope is not proof of one national assembly.

organizer.summary: S003 identifies money changers as actors but names no formal organizer of its reported assemblies. S014 names the Herat money-changers’ union and national association in the work-strike context, without linking either to the S003 assemblies.

demands.summary: S003 reports opposition to the Central Bank plan to replace individual licenses with company licensing. S014 directly describes that state policy and says money changers demanded that the government address/review it; this supports the policy grievance but does not itself report an assembly.

participants.summary: Neither source reports a count of assembled people. S014’s more than 430 individual licenses and five company conversions count licenses/businesses, not participants.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: S003 explicitly reports public assemblies but gives no attendance. S014 reports a nationwide work stoppage and license/business counts only, not a public assembly or turnout; the threshold remains unverified.

protester_violence.summary: The article does not establish protester violence or an explicit absence.

state_response.summary: Accommodation is coded yes because the money changers actually met President Ghani and the strike ended after the meeting; all other response dimensions remain unknown.

state_accommodation.summary: The report says money changers met President Ghani on Feb. 21 and that the strike ended after this meeting, with the government promising to address their problems within a week. This establishes reception/negotiation, not policy implementation.

state_arrests.summary: No arrests related to the gatherings are reported.

state_beatings.summary: No state beatings related to the gatherings are reported.

state_crowd_dispersal.summary: No state crowd-dispersal action is reported.

state_ignore.summary: No explicit state refusal/avoidance is reported; the article instead reports a meeting.

state_killings.summary: No state killing related to the gatherings is reported.

state_shootings.summary: No state firearm shooting related to the gatherings is reported.

notes: This candidate is based on reported public gatherings, not the nationwide work stoppage alone. Salam Watandar reports an initial gathering at Sarai Shahzada and later gatherings on Feb. 20 in Kabul and some provinces, but no count or site list; whether these comprise one national action or separate local events is unresolved. The article gives conflicting onset clues (“16 days before Feb. 21” and “18 Dalw/Bahman”), so only month precision is retained. A Feb. 21 meeting with President Ghani is an actual state reception/negotiation and supports accommodation=yes; the promised one-week remedy is not proof of concession or implementation. The strike’s end does not establish the gatherings’ physical end. Parstoday S014 separately supplies Feb. 6 work-stoppage/policy context, but reports no public assembly or attendance and is not used to establish the S003 gathering, turnout or exact date; its Radio Dari attribution and Pars Today page byline leave written-origin dependence unresolved.
open_questions: Find attendance at the initial gathering and Feb. 20 assemblies; do not infer from number of workers or closed exchanges.
Resolve the relative/Gregorian-calendar onset discrepancy without inventing a day.
Determine whether the separate locations and repeat gatherings were one coordinated event or distinct local assemblies.
Physical end of the public assemblies is unknown; strike end on Feb. 21 is separate.
Check whether the one-week government response was implemented; keep other state responses unknown.
The article cites a presidential spokesperson’s statement/tweet; seek independent contemporary reporting without assuming shared source or independent confirmation.
